acceptance: When `evolve doctor live <driver>` fails, it keeps the final pane of the probe in a named file and prints the path. A unit test pins this for a fake driver that fails.
`evolve doctor live codex-tmux` reports LIVE OK on codex-cli 0.162.1. A fixture of the 0.162.1 pane, taken from the kept capture, pins the submit fix in the codex manifest or driver.
`evolve clihealth usage codex` shows the codex quota windows. The codex manifest gains `controls.usage.windows`, pinned by a fixture of the real codex `/usage` screen.
fix: Three steps, in this order. (1) Make `doctor live` keep the final pane of a failed probe, for every CLI, so that a screen change can be read through the bridge and not through a raw session. (2) Read the kept codex pane, find why the prompt submit wedges on codex-cli 0.162.1, and fix it in the manifest data first, with Go code only if data cannot express it. (3) Add `controls.usage.windows` to the codex manifest from a fixture of the real codex `/usage` screen. Every query goes through the bridge (docs/plans/bridge-factory-2026-10.md, ADR-0137 in PR #914). New and changed functions reach 100% coverage.
source: console, operator request 'check if codex is fine' and 'Queue the codex fix', 2026-10-17
summary: On 2026-10-17, `evolve doctor live codex-tmux` failed with rc=81 submit_wedged on codex-cli 0.162.1: the prompt did not submit after 3 resends. `evolve clihealth usage codex` read no window, because the codex manifest has a `/usage` command but no `windows` parse spec. `doctor live` keeps no pane capture of a failed probe, so the screen that wedged cannot be read through the bridge. Codex is out of every routing chain, so no phase is affected today.
title: The codex live probe wedges on submit (codex-cli 0.162.1), codex has no usage windows, and doctor live keeps no pane of a failed probe
